We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction to produce target molecule. The template 1209837 seems to be a carbonyl-ene type? The retro template: [C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH] >> C-C(=C)-C(=O)-O-[C:2](-[C:3])-[C:4]. That is forward: carbonyl-ene forms product with OH. In retrosynthesis, we break product into a carbonyl precursor with an alkene and carbonyl.

Our target has a cyclopentanol fused? Let's examine target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

So there is a cyclopentanol (five-membered ring) attached to a fluorinated carbon (CF3) and a chiral center. Also an exocyclic alkene attached to aromatic phenyl.

The retro template likely splits the cyclopentanol into a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene (the exocyclic double bond). The precursor would be something like: a ketone with an allylic alkene? Let's apply template to target to get precursors.

Use apply_template tool.
